role: Marching rays and signed distance fields: step along the ray by the distance to the nearest surface until it is under a small epsilon; the sphere SDF length(p) - r.
adaptation: Kept as blobField() and marchSurface(). New: the march runs in the proxy box's object space and only between the box's entry and exit (slab interval), with an explicit hit flag, a step budget from the Steps control and a Newton refinement on the surface.

role: The first raymarch loop (MAX_STEPS, MAX_DIST, SURFACE_DIST) and the ray origin and direction from a fixed camera.
adaptation: The ray no longer comes from a fixed vec3(0, 0, 5) camera and a screen uv: each pixel of a rasterized proxy box is turned back into its camera ray with TouchDesigner's own matrices (uTDMats[].camProjInverse at depth 0 gives the point where the ray crosses the near plane), so any perspective, orthographic or blended camera, lens and object transform works, and glass nearer than the near plane is clipped. MAX_DIST becomes the box exit.

role: Normals from the SDF gradient (getNormal with central differences) and dot-product diffuse lighting.
adaptation: fieldNormal() uses Inigo Quilez's four-sample tetrahedron estimate (the article points to his normals article, line 325) and transforms it to world space with the inverse transpose of the object-to-world map. The glass look replaces plain diffuse.

role: Union by min() and the polynomial smoothmin(a, b, k) that makes shapes melt together 'like liquids'.
adaptation: smoothMin() is the same polynomial with an explicit zero-width branch (k < 1e-4 returns min), because the archived form divides by k. Each blob's k fades with it, so fractional counts grow blobs in smoothly. Property test smooth_min_stays_finite_without_holes.

role: Move, rotate and scale a raymarched object by transforming the sampling point the opposite way; scaling needs the distance corrected.
adaptation: Applied to the whole ray instead of each sample: the ray is moved into object space with the inverse of the Geometry COMP's affine transform (origin and axes captured through TDDeform in the vertex stage). Hits are exact in object space, so no per-sample scale correction is needed; path lengths are converted back to scene units.

role: Archived scene behind the smooth-min demo (scene5): sdSphere, smin, three spheres merging, raymarch loop and getNormal.
adaptation: Read with demos.py show/export. The archived scene adds Perlin displacement to the distance (line 106), which can break the distance bound; here ripples use a product of sines with a known slope and the march step shrinks by that slope (stepScale()).

role: Transparency by sampling a render of the scene behind the mesh at the pixel's screen position.
adaptation: Through the core study: the Refraction TOP, sampled at gl_FragCoord * uTDGeneral.viewport.zw. The archived steps (lines 109-114) snapshot 'the entire scene (the other meshes, the background, etc.)' with the mesh hidden; that assumes an opaque background and also captures meshes in front of the glass. New in the independent review round: the Refraction TOP's alpha is kept, so a render with a transparent background passes the later composite's background through clear glass. Meshes in front still appear inside the glass (no depth test); the README says to leave them out of that render.

role: refract() of the eye vector by the surface normal, used as a screen offset.
adaptation: Extended to two interfaces with a real path: bend in at the front surface, march inside to the far wall, bend out there (total internal reflection falls back to reflect), continue Backdrop distance, project with the camera. At IOR 1 every path stays on the pixel's own camera ray (property test ior1_is_invisible).

role: Chromatic dispersion with per-channel IORs and extra samples per loop.
adaptation: Through the core study's spectral loop (one read per sample, smooth R/G/B weights). New: each sample reads a mipmap level as wide as the gap between neighbouring colours on screen, because real lens paths spread colours far enough to show separate copies.

role: Saturation by mixing with luminance.
adaptation: Unchanged from the core (saturateColour).

role: Squared Blinn-Phong specular and a fresnel glow.
adaptation: Unchanged from the core (highlights).

role: Back-face rendering for the far side of the object.
adaptation: Not used. The far wall comes from the interior march through the same distance field, so the true thickness is measured in one pass without a second render.

role: Beer's law: light through a medium falls off as exp(-density x distance).
adaptation: absorption() applies it per colour channel to the measured path length inside the glass, so thick merged regions tint more than thin rims.

role: The archived final refraction scene (16 samples, six IORs).
adaptation: Read through the core study; nothing copied directly.
